name: Avukana Buddha Statue
description: A magnificent 12-meter standing Buddha statue carved out of a massive granite rock face in the 5th century during the reign of King Dhatusena.

name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
description: One of the Atamasthana sacred sites, this sacred fig tree was planted in 288 BC and is known as the oldest human-planted tree in the world with a known planting date.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
description: A magnificent white stupa built by King Dutugemunu in 140 BC, housing sacred relics of the Buddha. It is one of the highest monuments built in the ancient world.

name: Thuparamaya
description: The first Buddhist stupa constructed in Sri Lanka after the introduction of Buddhism, built during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (3rd century BC).

name: Lovamahapaya (Brazen Palace)
description: An ancient 9-story chapter house built by King Dutugemunu, featuring 1,600 stone pillars that once supported a massive bronze-roofed structure.

name: Abhayagiri Dagaba
description: A colossal ancient stupa and central monastic complex established in the 2nd century BC, celebrated for its advanced architectural engineering.

name: Jetavanaramaya
description: An enormous ancient brick stupa built by King Mahasena. At 122 meters, it was once the third-tallest structure in the ancient world.

name: Mirisavetiya Stupa
description: Built by King Dutugemunu after his victory, this historic stupa marks the spot where his scepter containing sacred Buddha relics could not be moved.

name: Lankarama
description: A stupa built in the 1st century BC by King Valagamba, originally housed inside a circular Vatadage with carved stone pillars.

name: Samadhi Buddha Statue
description: A famous 4th-century granite statue depicting the Buddha in the Dhyana Mudra meditation posture located within Mahamevnawa Park.

name: Isurumuniya Lovers & Temple
description: A rock temple built near Tissa Wewa, renowned worldwide for its 6th-century stone bas-relief carving of 'Isurumuniya Lovers'.

name: Ranmasu Uyana (Royal Pleasure Gardens)
description: Ancient royal gardens featuring sophisticated stone bathing pools, royal pavilions, and the mysterious 'Sakwala Chakraya' star gate carving.

name: Mihintale Sacred Mountain
description: The birthplace of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, featuring 1,840 granite steps, Aradhana Gala peak, Kantaka Cetiya, and panoramic ancient valley views.

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage
description: A remarkably preserved circular relic house inside the Dalada Maluwa, featuring intricately carved moonstones, guardstones, and four seated Buddha statues.

name: Gal Viharaya (Rock Temple)
description: A world-famous rock temple featuring four monumental Buddha statues carved seamlessly into a single granite cliff face by King Parakramabahu I.

name: Rankoth Vehera
description: The largest stupa in Polonnaruwa, standing at 54 meters tall, modeled directly after the colossal ancient stupas of Anuradhapura.

name: Lankatilaka Image House
description: A massive 12th-century brick cathedral-like structure with 17-meter high walls housing a headless standing Buddha statue.

name: Royal Palace of King Parakramabahu
description: The ruins of a magnificent 7-story royal palace that once contained 1,000 chambers, supported by thick brick walls and stone pillars.

name: Nissanka Latha Mandapaya
description: A unique stone structure featuring carved granite pillars shaped like curving lotus stalks surrounding a small stupa.

name: Tiwanka Image House
description: Famous for its rare 12th-century frescoes and a standing Buddha statue depicted in the 'Tiwanka' (thrice-bent) posture.

name: Pothgul Viharaya & Parakramabahu Statue
description: An ancient monastery library complex and a nearby 3.5-meter stone statue carved into a rock face believed to depict King Parakramabahu I.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa)
description: Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist temple, housing the relic of the tooth of the Buddha within a golden-roofed royal palace complex.

name: Gadaladeniya Rajamaha Viharaya
description: A 14th-century South Indian Dravidian style stone temple constructed atop a flat rock outcrop during the Gampola Kingdom era.

name: Lankatilaka Viharaya (Kandy)
description: A majestic 14th-century rock-top temple combining Buddhist and Hindu shrines under one roof with sweeping views of the surrounding hills.

name: Embekke Devalaya
description: Famous worldwide for its masterfully carved wooden pillars depicting swans, wrestlers, soldiers, and mythical creatures in the Digge (Drummers' Hall).

name: Degaldoruwa Raja Maha Viharaya
description: A famous cave temple renowned for housing some of Sri Lanka's finest 18th-century Kandyan style ceiling murals painted by Silvatgama.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple (Golden Temple)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage complex of five sprawling rock caves filled with 153 Buddha statues and 2,100 square meters of colorful ceiling murals.

name: Nalanda Gedige
description: An ancient 8th-century stone temple built in the South Indian Pallava style, unique for its blend of Hindu tantric carvings and Buddhist architecture at the geographical center of Sri Lanka.

name: Aluvihare Rock Temple
description: The historic cave monastery where the Tipitaka (Buddhist canon) was first committed to writing on palm leaves (Ola leaves) in the 1st century BC.

name: Galle Fort & Lighthouse
description: A UNESCO World Heritage 16th-century Dutch colonial rampart city overlooking the ocean, filled with cobblestone lanes, boutiques, bastions, and the famous white lighthouse.

name: Star Fort Matara
description: A unique 6-pointed star-shaped Dutch fort constructed in 1765, featuring a moat, drawbridge, and well-preserved coral stone walls.

name: Fort Frederick
description: A Portuguese and Dutch fort built in 1623 on a peninsula overlooking Trincomalee harbor, housing wild spotted deer and leading up to Koneswaram Temple.

name: Koneswaram Temple (Temple of a Thousand Pillars)
description: A revered classical Hindu Kovil standing atop Swami Rock cliff edge, offering breathtaking 360-degree views of the Indian Ocean.

name: Jaffna Fort
description: A massive pentagonal Dutch fort built in 1680 out of white coral stone, standing gracefully on the edge of the Jaffna lagoon.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: The landmark Hindu temple of Jaffna featuring a majestic golden Gopuram tower, sacred pools, and elaborate daily chariot rituals.

name: Nagadeepa Purana Viharaya
description: An ancient island temple on Nainativu Island where the Buddha is believed to have visited to settle a dispute over a gem-studded throne.

name: Keerimalai Naguleswaram Kovil & Holy Springs
description: An ancient coastal Hindu Kovil and adjacent natural freshwater mineral springs situated directly next to the ocean edge.

name: Dambakola Patuna
description: The historic ancient port where Sangamitta Theri landed in Sri Lanka bearing the sacred sapling of the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi tree.

name: Point Pedro Lighthouse
description: A historic white lighthouse standing at the northernmost point of Sri Lanka, marking the coastal boundary of the Jaffna peninsula.

name: Mannar Fort
description: A 16th-century square Portuguese and Dutch fort overlooking the Mannar causeway with four bastions and historic coastal stone walls.

name: Thiruketheeswaram Kovil
description: One of the five ancient Ishwarams (sacred Shiva temples) of Sri Lanka, situated near the ancient port of Mantai.

name: Doric House (Doric Bungalow Arippu)
description: The historic ruins of the first British Governor Frederick North's residence built in 1804 in classical Greek-revival style overlooking Arippu beach.

name: Baobab Tree Mannar
description: A massive, ancient Baobab tree planted by Arab traders over 700 years ago, featuring a trunk circumference of nearly 20 meters.

name: Kataragama Sacred City (Tissamaharama / Kataragama)
description: A multi-religious pilgrimage site sacred to Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, and Indigenous Vedda people along the Menik Ganga river.

name: Buduruwagala Rock Sculptures
description: An 8th-century sanctuary featuring seven colossal Mahayana Buddhist statues carved in high relief into a massive cliff in the forest.

name: Maligawila Elephant & Giant Buddha Statue
description: The tallest free-standing ancient limestone Buddha statue in Sri Lanka, standing at 11.5 meters, carved in the 7th century.

name: Seruwawila Mangala Raja Maha Viharaya
description: An ancient 2nd-century BC stupa built by King Kavantissa, enshrining the Lalata Dhatu (sacred forehead bone relic) of the Buddha.

name: Girihandu Seya (Thiriyaya)
description: Considered Sri Lanka's oldest stupa, built on a hilltop at Thiriyaya by merchants Tapassu and Bhalluka to enshrine sacred hair relics.

name: Velgam Viharaya (Vilgam Vehera)
description: A historic ancient Buddhist temple complex that was protected and patronized by Chola rulers in the 11th century.

name: Batticaloa Fort
description: A quaint 4-bastion coastal fort built by the Portuguese in 1628, situated on a island near the Batticaloa lagoon.

name: Mamangam Pillaiyar Kovil
description: An ancient Hindu Kovil dedicated to Lord Ganesha, renowned for its annual festival draw and sacred temple pool.

name: Deegavapi Stupa
description: An ancient sacred stupa built by King Saddhatissa in the 2nd century BC, undergoing major archaeological restoration.

name: Muhudu Maha Viharaya
description: An ancient coastal temple complex at Arugam Bay featuring stone statues of the Buddha and Royal figures among the beach dunes.

name: Magul Maha Viharaya
description: An ancient forest temple famous for its beautifully preserved stone Vatadage, moonstone, and royal wedding hall ruins.
